feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond scale metrics, and could be streamlined for sharper impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and sustained performance.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and marketable.  
- Generally clean writing and structure: concise profile, relevant skills, and experience bullets that are easy to follow.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable impact such as engagement growth, conversion improvements, cost savings, efficiency gains, or adoption rates.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-Oxford-comma lists); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent work without repeating the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten the first sentence for smoother flow.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce list-heavy wording.
- Emphasize senior-level value: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, governance, analytics, and workflow design for mission-driven organizations.
- Add public-sector/advocacy context, which is a clear throughline in the experience section.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, digital transformation, and platform modernization for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS strategy, editorial workflows, analytics, and cross-functional coordination. Strong background in public-sector and advocacy communications, translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the list more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper terms and favor higher-value leadership language over generic phrasing.
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Multi-channel communications leadership” for grammatical consistency and stronger seniority.
- Consider: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web & CMS management • Editorial operations & governance • Workflow & systems design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, align wording with recent work by emphasizing enterprise web, governance, optimization, and cross-functional leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “stakeholder coordination,” “advocacy messaging”) and much of Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills; keep competencies focused on hard/functional strengths.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level impact, transformation, and only the newest/highest-value work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with sharper impact language: “modernized,” “streamlined,” “architected,” “launched,” “optimized.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Architect digital workflows, analytics, and governance improvements supporting coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Build Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Lead AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success, or toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this item focused on consulting impact and new initiatives.
- Microsite and AI search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget across enterprise platforms.”
- Combine and tighten web modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership outcome-focused: replace “reaching tens of thousands…” with a metric on growth, engagement, deliverability, or campaign performance if available.
- Strengthen impact language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and relies on “helped” language that weakens ownership. Tighten it around operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth to show clear step-up before the director role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Replace weaker bullets with action + outcome framing: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Publishing workflows” and “coordination” also appear in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating governance language too heavily.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated language tied to enterprise leadership:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” to align with recent experience and avoid vague leadership wording.
- Use “audience-centered” or “user-centered” instead of “audience-focused” for a more current, strategic tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) for work experience rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Cut lower-signal items if space is tight; “WordPress” may matter less than enterprise modernization unless target roles explicitly want it.
- If possible, tie to scale elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites” rather than listing platforms alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:

- Consider adding one impact cue if space allows: **Built analytics infrastructure to support strategic decision-making across high-traffic public-sector web properties**

- This nearly duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; avoid repeating the same tools in both places.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one for strategy, the other for systems.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than just names: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing via GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially used in recent roles; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep terminology consistent with the CV’s leadership tone: use **CMS platforms** or **Web platforms** rather than a generic tool list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience; avoid overemphasizing it in multiple sections unless adding distinct context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied implementation: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively used in recent roles/projects; if possible add specificity elsewhere in CV (e.g., GTM for analytics tagging, Workers for edge logic/prototyping)
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies; this section should stay tool-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and strongest tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams | Legacy/project use: Basecamp”
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show applied use: “Airtable (content ops databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project workflow management).”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” to better match your leadership profile.
- Drop weaker/older tools if space is tight; Basecamp feels least important relative to recent enterprise work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools and may add little unless you need keyword coverage.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since recent roles already emphasize email leadership, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use without repeating work history, e.g. **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member communications**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email automation, newsletter and member engagement workflows)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or campaign leadership here; those are already covered in recent NACo roles.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications elsewhere, so keep this item limited to email/member platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, add scale or output metrics to show early impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize promotion, team-building, and concrete delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split execution from leadership: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics: volume of videos/livestreams, audience reach, engagement lift, production turnaround, or process improvements.
- Tighten the closing: “Provided day-to-day supervision and production guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or early-building that program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel coverage already stated more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination and digital content development; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work” with clearer scope: county innovation initiatives, policy communications, research projects, stakeholder-facing materials.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types/volume of multimedia assets produced.
- Keep it to one concise bullet or sentence so it doesn’t compete with stronger later digital roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Podcast/video production themes recur later, so position this as the first/launch milestone rather than ongoing channel leadership.
